summary: The study describes the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of ultrathin nickel sulfide (NiS_x) films using bis(N,N′-di-tert-butylacetamidinato)nickel(II) (Ni(amd)2) and hydrogen sulfide (H2S) as precursors. The ALD process was optimized to achieve self-limiting growth over a temperature range of 125−225 °C. The films were characterized for their electrocatalytic activity in hydrogen evolution reactions, showing promising performance with overpotentials of 440 mV in acidic conditions and 576 mV in pH 7 phosphate buffer. The study highlights the potential of ALD-grown NiS_x as a water-compatible electrocatalyst.
evidence: The text states: 'To this end, we employed atomic layer deposition (ALD), a preeminent method to fabricate uniform and conformal films, to construct thin films of nickel sulﬁde (NiS_x) using bis(N,N′-di-tert-butylacetamidinato)nickel(II) (Ni(amd)2) vapor and hydrogen sulﬁde gas.' It also mentions: 'The ALD-synthesized films were characterized using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) methods. To assess the electrocatalytic activity of NiS_x for evolution of molecular hydrogen, films were grown on conductive-glass supports. Overpotentials at a current density of 10 mA/cm2 were recorded in both acidic and pH 7 phosphate buffer aqueous reaction media and found to be 440 and 576 mV, respectively, with very low NiS_x loading.'
